title: D.4 Quantum Physics
subject: IBDP Physics
introduction: Quantum physics studies the behaviour of matter and radiation at atomic and subatomic scales. At these scales, particles show both wave-like and particle-like properties. Quantum theory explains phenomena such as the photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, electron behaviour and modern technologies including lasers and semiconductors.
learning_objectives: Understand the quantum nature of light.

definitions.meaning: A discrete packet of energy or matter that exists in specific amounts.
A particle of electromagnetic radiation carrying a fixed amount of energy.
A fixed energy state that an electron can occupy inside an atom.
The movement of an electron between different energy levels by absorbing or emitting energy.
The idea that particles and radiation can show both wave and particle properties.
The minimum energy required to remove an electron from a material surface.

core_concepts.heading: Quantisation of Energy
core_concepts.explanation: Quantum physics shows that energy is not continuous at atomic scales. Energy exists in specific packets called quanta.

core_concepts.heading: Photon Energy
core_concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation consists of photons. The energy of each photon depends on its frequency.

core_concepts.heading: Atomic Energy Levels
core_concepts.explanation: Electrons in atoms can only exist at specific energy levels. They absorb or emit photons when moving between these levels.

core_concepts.heading: Wave Particle Duality
core_concepts.explanation: Experiments show that light behaves as both a wave and a particle depending on how it is measured.

formulas.name: Photon Energy
formulas.explanation: Photon energy is directly proportional to frequency. Higher frequency radiation contains higher energy photons.

formulas.name: Photon Energy Using Wavelength
formulas.explanation: This equation connects photon energy with wavelength. Shorter wavelength radiation has higher energy.

formulas.name: Photoelectric Equation

variables.Ek: maximum kinetic energy of emitted electron

formulas.explanation: Photon energy is used to overcome the work function and provide kinetic energy to emitted electrons.

photoelectric_effect.explanation: The photoelectric effect occurs when electrons are emitted from a metal surface after absorbing electromagnetic radiation with enough energy.

observations: Electrons are emitted only when frequency is above a threshold frequency.
Increasing intensity increases the number of emitted electrons.
Increasing frequency increases the kinetic energy of emitted electrons.
Emission occurs almost instantly when the threshold is exceeded.

photoelectric_effect.explanation: The threshold frequency is the minimum frequency required for photons to remove electrons from a material.

atomic_spectra.explanation: Atoms produce specific wavelengths of light because electrons can only occupy specific energy levels.
An emission spectrum is produced when electrons fall from higher energy levels to lower energy levels and release photons.
An absorption spectrum is produced when electrons absorb specific photon energies and move to higher energy levels.

electron_transitions.explanation: An electron absorbs a photon and moves to a higher energy level when the photon energy matches the energy difference.
An electron releases a photon when it moves from a higher energy level to a lower energy level.
The energy difference between two atomic levels equals the energy of the emitted or absorbed photon.

worked_examples.question: Calculate the energy of a photon with frequency 5 × 10¹⁴ Hz.
A metal has a work function of 2 eV. Explain what happens when a photon with energy 3 eV hits the surface.
solution: Photon energy is greater than the work function.
The extra energy becomes kinetic energy of the electron.
worked_examples.answer: An electron is emitted with 1 eV kinetic energy.

matter_waves.explanation: Louis de Broglie proposed that particles such as electrons also have wave properties. This means matter can show both particle and wave behaviour.

matter_waves.name: de Broglie Wavelength
matter_waves.explanation: The wavelength of a particle decreases as its momentum increases. Small particles such as electrons show noticeable wave behaviour.
Electron diffraction experiments show that electrons produce interference patterns, proving their wave nature.

uncertainty_principle.explanation: It is impossible to know the exact position and momentum of a particle at the same time. Greater accuracy in one quantity causes greater uncertainty in the other.
The uncertainty principle becomes important at atomic and subatomic scales.

quantum_applications.explanation: Lasers use stimulated emission, where atoms release photons with the same frequency and phase.
Quantum behaviour of electrons allows the operation of transistors, computer chips and electronic devices.
Electron microscopes use the short wavelength of electrons to create highly detailed images.
Solar cells use the photoelectric effect to convert photon energy into electrical energy.

quantum_models.explanation: The particle model explains photons as packets of energy and particles as objects with measurable properties.
The wave model explains interference, diffraction and other wave behaviours.
The quantum model combines wave and particle behaviour to describe matter and radiation at small scales.

common_mistakes: Thinking photons have no energy because they have no rest mass.
Forgetting that photon energy depends on frequency.
Mixing work function and kinetic energy.
Using wavelength instead of frequency in photon equations.
ib_exam_tips: Remember E = hf for photon energy calculations.
Explain the photoelectric effect using photons.
State that energy levels in atoms are quantised.
Use conservation of energy in electron transition questions.
Explain wave-particle duality using experimental evidence.

hl_extension.explanation: Particles have a probability of passing through energy barriers even when classical physics predicts they cannot.
Quantum mechanics describes particles using probability distributions rather than exact paths.
A photon causes an excited atom to emit another identical photon, allowing laser production.

practice_questions.question: What is a photon?
practice_questions.answer: A photon is a packet of electromagnetic energy.

practice_questions.question: Why does increasing frequency increase photon energy?
practice_questions.answer: Photon energy is directly proportional to frequency according to E = hf.

practice_questions.question: Explain wave-particle duality.
practice_questions.answer: Matter and radiation show both wave and particle properties depending on the experiment.

summary: Quantum physics explains the behaviour of matter and radiation at atomic scales. Concepts such as photons, energy quantisation, the photoelectric effect and wave-particle duality explain modern technologies including lasers, electronics and medical equipment.
